He had expected Aravalli to be wiped out of the Universe today, but for it to still stand—and worse, for Lord Orravyn to appear to stop Lady Seraphielle and shamefully send her away—
He could tell what Lady Seraphielle was feeling, and he...
He had no intention of getting on her bad side right now.
So if she said something needed to be done, it was his responsibility to make sure itdidget done.
Therefore, Lord Light turned towards the Light Born Leader that he had sent away before and—
"Gather your men."
He commanded.
Lord Light only had control over all the Light Borns, not the other followers of Light, and this operation—
This needed Light’s complete power.
The Light Born Leader nodded with a solemn look, waiting for Lord Light to speak.
And Lord Light did—
"From this day forth, the Light Worlds will enter Complete Lockdown."
Lord Light announced.
The Light Borns frowned in confusion.
"What...?"
The Leader blinked.
Complete Lockdown?
What did that even mean?
The very idea behind it was so absurd that he couldn’t even imagine it.
But...
It was happening.
"Trade routes will be sealed.
Gates will shut down.
Warp-lanes will be chained.
No merchant convoy, no pilgrim fleet, no wandering mercenary band will cross our borders without Lady Seraphielle’s approval."
Light Borns widened their eyes in shock.
They glanced at Seraphielle, as if trying to confirm whether what they were hearing was actually her decision, but the Infinity of Light only stared at the temple around her.
As if she was checking if her temple was reconstructed properly or if the work done needed... punishment.
Lord Light, on the other hand, continued—
"From this moment onward, no being living under Light is permitted to leave Light Territory.
Not for profit.
Not for curiosity.
Not for ’information.’
Not for love.
If they wish to travel, they may travel within our dominion.
If they wish to trade, they may trade among our faithful.
If they wish to learn, they may learn from Light—because Light has no shortage of truth."
Light Borns stayed silent.
None dared to stop Lord Light or ask a question, no matter how absurd it all sounded.
"Trades that require abilities of other Factions are no longer needed.
As for artifacts and relics we absolutely need—
We ourselves will procure them and supply them to the people at the same price.
But Light’s people must learn how to live without assistance from others.
Light’s people must become independent."
Lord Light took a brief pause, as if letting those words echo throughout the temple and be registered into the Light Borns’ heads.
"No foreign being—not from Balance, Eternity, Darkness, or even independent of any of the Factions—will be permitted entry into our Territory."
Finally, Lord Light looked right at the Light Born Leader, as if he was giving a message, a message he needed to relay to the people.
"The Anomaly does not win by strength alone.
He wins by rot, whispers, and contamination.
He wins by letting doubt slip into the cracks.
Cracks that form even with the monthly memory scans."
Then, Lord Light lowered his voice.
"So we will remove the cracks."
He declared directly.
"And you will ensure the cracks are removed smoothly."
He spoke as he looked at the Light Born Leader.
"Do whatever you require.
You have Lady Seraphielle’s complete permission.
It doesn’t matter how many you need to kill, enslave, or threaten.
Do what you must.
Make sure the Worlds follow.
And any world that delays implementation—make sure they understand the consequences of being... negligent."
Lord Light spoke with a meaningful look on his face, a look that the Light Born Leader understood almost instantly.
Lord Light nodded when he noticed that glow of understanding in his eyes, then—
"Make sure people understand that this is not fear.
This is discipline.
This is Light purifying its structure.
A house under siege does not leave its doors open because closing them feels impolite.
Make sure that people understand that we will not ’debate’ with filth.
We will not ’explain’ ourselves to those who thirst for scandal.
We will not allow... the impure to smear our banners and then claim they touched truth."
Lord Light then raised his chin with that familiar arrogant gaze, and with him, the entire temple seemed like it was floating in the air—
"Light does not grovel.
Light does not chase rumors.
Light does not beg for belief."
After a short pause—
"Light protects what is its own.
And right now, what’s important is to protect the Faith.
Unfortunate things have been happening, things that have been affecting the Faith, and Light won’t just sit back and let it happen."

Lord Light’s gaze then turned towards Seraphielle, almost as if confirming whether she wanted to actually go forward with it, but again, Seraphielle acted like she wasn’t even listening, like her focus was still on the temple—and that was all Lord Light needed to see.
He gulped slightly before turning back towards the Light Borns, who themselves had heavy looks on their faces, but none of them said anything, and Lord Light continued—
"If they wish to call this isolation, let them.
If they wish to call this control, let them.
Words are cheap outside our walls.
And inside our walls—
We will be the ones who control those words.
We will have Order.
We will have stability.
We will have loyalty."
Then, after another pause, Lord Light spoke again—
"And if any among our own believe they need foreign tongues to tell them what Light is—
then they have already decided they do not deserve Light’s protection."
The Light Borns nodded at those words—not because they understood them; even they could tell what was being done here.
They just understood that this was what they were going to feed the people, and after some level of ’convincing’, implementing it shouldn’t be very difficult.
"Go."
Lord Light commanded, nodding at the Light Borns meaningfully.
The Light Born Leader nodded back and then—him, together with the rest of the Light Borns—
They all disappeared.
The only ones now remaining in the Temple were Lord Light and the Infinity of Light.
Lord Light turned towards Seraphielle, in case she had something to say.
And Seraphielle—
She finally stopped staring at the temple and turned towards Lord Light.
"You did well."
She complimented.
"I only did what was needed of me to do."
Lord Light answered as he bowed his head.
Seraphielle smiled at those words—
"You do not have to lie."
She spoke directly.
Lord Light froze, flinching in fear.
Seraphielle, however, just chuckled and—
"If you do not agree with the decision I made, you can talk to me.
That is the reason I created you.
You are created by my subconscious; the powers you have are mine.
If you disagree with me, that means a part ofmeis disagreeing with myself."
Lord Light looked at her, slightly confused, and Seraphielle revealed the complete truth without hiding anything.
"I am not sealing our worlds to stop the words regarding Anomaly’s actions from spreading."
"What...?"
Lord Light frowned in confusion.
This wasn’t being done to control information...?
Then why...
Before he could even form his thoughts any further, Seraphielle corrected him—
"I did not say I am not doing this to control information.
That, I admit to.
But the information about the Anomaly isn’t my main focus."
"If not Anomaly... then what is...
Lady Seraphielle planning...?"
Lord Light asked after a slight hesitation, and Seraphielle—
Her face turned much more solemn.
"War."
She announced.
"Against the other Three Infinities."
And Lord Light—
His eyes widened in absolute terror.
War...?
They were preparing for... war?
And that too, not against the Anomaly, but the other three Infinities?
What...?

chapters.title: Chapter 2285: Everything was falling apart.
paragraphs: The order was given and then—
It happened.
The entire Universe came to an abrupt halt, the gates that had been opened to the entire Universe for trade for trillions of years began to close.
And its impact—
It was huge.
The border worlds had it the worst, they were the ones who were most active when it came to trading outside the domain of Light.
It had become the reason they thrived.
But now—
That trading was banned. The outbound travel was suspended. Orders to turn away foreign ships were given.
It had become obvious.
The Light Worlds were now in complete lockdown.
The outsiders that were in the Light Territories were offered seventy-two hours to leave, and if they did not leave in the given time, force would be used.
Light made it very clear.
And the rule was the same regardless of who you were or what you belonged to, be it the Eternity Faction, Darkness Faction, the Balance Faction, or even those who didn’t belong to any Faction.
Light Worlds were completely isolated, and the worlds they could now interact with were... those who were part of the same faction.
It affected business, reputation, and anything or everything related to Light.
The Light called it a ’purification of borders,’ but the Universe—
They only saw the truth, the truth that Light was trying to hide its wounds behind curtains.
The Light Borns who implemented these rules did not ask for permission from the worlds, they didn’t need to.
They simply sent their men to every single Light World, making sure their words were received and properly understood.
And with that—
The same order was given to every single world, at the same time.
"Henceforth—
All outbound travel is forbidden.
All inbound travel is forbidden.
All trade must remain internal only.
All foreign contracts must be suspended."
There were more, several more in fact.
The talks about making Light independent of the Universe, making the Universe realize the importance of Light, making Light self-sustaining, making Light ’filth-free,’ and more.
It was clear that the Light Borns were given a direct script, a script written with the intentions of fooling the World Leaders.
And the World Leaders knew that—

They knew that this was nothing more than Light’s attempt to take more control. Of course, it was no different than what happened most of the time; all of Light’s actions, in one way or another, were taken to benefit Light.
This, however, was a bit too obvious; it could even be called desperate.
So much so that even the Leaders of the Lower Level Worlds could sense it.
But...
Did that change anything?
No.
The Worlds complied.
The reason was simple—an absurdly strong enemy was after them and they had no plans of being left alone in the Universe in that state.
Not to mention...
Rejecting the beings of Light that were sent to their worlds didn’t seem a wise choice.
After all, the moment they said anything, it wouldn’t be long before they were marked and labelled traitors. A label not a single one of them wanted.
The general people, on the other hand, had a surprisingly different reaction. Maybe it was the script the Light Borns were given working—
The people were... relieved.
They had been living with fear for years,
Fear of the Anomaly.
Fear of rumors.
Fear of being accused.
Fear of their... own minds.
But the moment the ’purification seal’ was announced—
The people felt... hope.
They didn’t know how this was going to help, they just felt a strong sense of hope simply because they could finally see Light making a move.
And since Light itself had moved, then it meant they would now be safe.
At least, that’s what they believed in their minds or... wanted to believe in their minds.

Cities held mass prayers, streets were filled with kneeling crowds. World Leaders saw it all happen from their rooms, watching their people foolishly chant the words that had been ingrained into them—
"Light protects us."
"We are loyal."
"We areclean."
But of course, the World Leaders could see it as well—
This wasn’t going to end well, there was no way.
And soon, it began.
The newfound relief and hope... began to fade away, just as most of the World Leaders expected.
The ’purification seal’ soon stopped feeling like a lockdown, and started to feel like a prison itself.
It had started to feel like a cage.
Merchants panicked when they realized they could no longer sell outside; entire dynasties depended on neutral markets. Families depended on routes that ran through Balance or Eternity.
Ships sat in docks forever.
Port workers lost jobs.
Trade cities grew quiet.
Then another, much bigger problem appeared—

Merchants were different from the rest; these were the beings who had spent their entire lives roaming around, setting up branches throughout the rest of the Universe. These were the people who spent more of their lives outside than back in their own homes—
And they were expected to just... sit down and never leave their world again?
It was impossible.
And these people felt... suffocated.
Many of these people had family outside Light Territory; those beings were completely cut off.
Almost all mercenaries living off foreign contracts were finished.
It was... hell.
And not just for the merchants or the people directly affected by the changes—even the other people who weren’t directly affected started to feel... strange.
And it wasn’t because of the economic collapse.
While implementing the change, Light ensured that did not happen; the resources they had gathered for trillions and trillions of years were now being used extensively to ensure the change was smooth.
But...
The suffocation was still there.
With the suffocation, the frustration rose higher, and every time the frustration became stronger, the beings of Light arrived—
For their monthly memory scans.
Leaving people with no choice but to swallow their frustration—no, they didn’t just swallow it; since they knew their memories were about to be scanned—
They... erased their frustration and arrived before Light, clean.
Outside the Light borders, the Universe reacted in waves.
Neutral worlds laughed first, some even mocking Light openly.
That looks... desperate.
I pity them.
Such words spread throughout the Universe.
And the worlds that belonged to the other three Supreme Factions?
Their reaction was even more extreme.
They not only openly mocked Light, they now felt... superior. Because Light was clearly failing at whatever they were doing.
Of course, they too took the brunt of Light Worlds leaving the economic market, but that was nowhere close to being caged inside their own homes.
It was clear that no force in the Universe thought highly of Light’s decision. People even began comparing Infinities; words about Seraphielle’s incompetence began to spread.
Yes, for the first time in the Universe, an Infinity was being insulted openly, even looked down upon.
After all, with Light Worlds out of the trade, prices changed everywhere, many trades collapsed, many forces took the brunt and fell.
The frustration became higher—not just in the worlds inside the Light Territory, those could still be controlled since Light now held all the information—but the rest of the worlds in the Universe?
Their worlds couldn’t be controlled.
And they...
They got even louder.
"If Light has nothing to hide? Why act like this?"
"Nothing to hide? Have you not seen the recordings? It’s obvious those hypocritical bastards are lying, they always have."
"Hypocrites. I am so glad our world didn’t join the Light’s faction, to be so rotten while representing peace.
Even the Darkness Faction is better than that, at least they are honest about what they crave."
These talks became normal, people who never once dared to call out any of the Supreme Factions were now openly bad-mouthing Light, louder than ever.
How could they not?
According to them, no being from the Light Worlds was around them; they could say whatever they wanted and Light wouldn’t know.
And what ruined Light’s reputation even further was—
That even after all this, even after Light Worlds had to face a complete lockdown and all the economic and emotional backlash that came with it—
The Anomaly’s attacks hadn’t stopped.
Even now, every single week, the Universe trembled, a Light World disappeared, and the recording was shown throughout the Universe.
It had almost become a ritual.
An open ritual where Light was humiliated in front of the entire Universe and its powerlessness was mocked.
The only difference was that before, the Light Worlds only learned about which world had perished after some time through the merchants or traders, and now, those worlds have no way of knowing.
The entire Universe was pitying Light Worlds, and the Light Faction itself?
It was... blacklisted by the people, fallen to a level where people cursed their enemies to become part of the Light Faction.
It had become a form of an insult.
And then—
More and more news began to travel—
News that... made a lot of sense.
In the past two weeks, five Light Worlds... had left the Light Faction.
Yes, it was happening.
The Light Worlds—
The pressure finally became more than what they could handle.
And everything—
Everything was falling apart.

chapters.title: Chapter 2286: The Plan.
paragraphs: "This is the fourteenth one."
An Eternal Level Light Born, Araya, walked into a room with a solemn look on her face. In front of her sat another Light Born, Lucian, another Eternal Level Light Born, and not just any Eternal—
He was the second strongest.
Well—
Now the strongest Light Born.
Yes, after Auren, it was him who was known for his strength, the only Light Born who could actually face Auren and not lose as pathetically as others did.
Lucian was strong, stronger than almost all the Light Borns, and with Auren now out of the picture, his importance only grew more.
But...
Lucian did not like that.
If it was any other situation, a situation where Auren somehow perished or was weakened and he replaced him, he wouldn’t have minded.
But with Light being targeted as strongly as it was right now—
Lucian feared that he too had become a target. He thought that Auren was taken out because he was the hope of Light.
The strongest being the Anomaly could defeat, so he did.
And now?
That being was him.
If Anomaly targeted him, the Light Borns who now had their hopes on him would feel crushed.
Of course, he was giving himself too much credit. No Light Born actually held any hopes on him, not when the one stronger than him was defeated without having much of a chance to fight.
Honestly, most Light Borns believed the Anomaly didn’t even know of his existence, and if he did, he didn’t really care.
But of course, they couldn’t say it out loud.
Not when the other party was stronger than them and held more power.
"That quickly?"
Lucian raised his eyebrow.
"It has only been two months since lockdown began. It clearly doesn’t have any effect."
He commented, letting go of the documents he was reading.
Araya did not say anything, she just stood still, thinking.
"How many does it make in total, just in this week?"
Lucian asked.
"This was the third."
Araya answered in a low voice. She knew it too, it wasn’t good news.
"Three in a single week.
It is happening fast.
Faster than we had expected, they are much more cowardly than we were expecting."
Again, Araya didn’t say anything.
Honestly, she understood.

The Light Worlds were in ultimate panic, their emotions were being played with. They were being locked in the name of being protected, and while it might have worked at some level, the issue was that even after going through what they were going through, even after abandoning their freedom, even after letting another being peek into their minds every single month—
They weren’t actually protected.
This was more about protecting Light’s reputation than protecting them, and after Light’s desperate action, it was becoming clearer and clearer.
It did not seem like Light cared about its people, and when every single one of their actions was only strengthening this point, how long would the worlds still be willing to serve under them?
At this point, it was no longer about loyalty either—
It was about fear.

The Worlds were scared to leave Light, not because they were scared of being targeted by Anomaly and being defenseless against him. Anomaly had already proved that Light’s protection did absolutely nothing to stop him.
It didn’t even slow him down.
They were scared of Light itself, of what Light might do if they decided to leave.

After all, because Light now controlled the information, the Worlds still did not know about the fourteen worlds that had already left Light. If they did, nothing would have stopped them from leaving too.
But...
There was only so much fear could actually make people do.
After constant suppression in almost every way, almost every single world would leave.
It was only a matter of time.
And both Light Borns present in the room knew that.
"How long do you think we have?"
Just when both Light Borns were thinking about everything that had happened, suddenly Lucian asked.
Araya looked at him, and for a moment, she didn’t say anything.
Both Light Borns obviously knew that the way things were going, all Light Worlds would leave the Light Faction, and the Faction would... perish.
And obviously, since they knew that, Lord Light and Seraphielle knew that before making this decision as well.
So why do it?
Why do something so... self-destructive?
The answer was simple.
Light wasn’t self-destructing, it was... preparing.

After everything that had happened, if there was one good thing that came for Light out of this, it was the fact that they now held complete control over the information that went around the Light Faction.
And together with this—
They also had control over what information regarding the Light Faction would travel to the rest of the Universe, which, right now, was... nothing.
Yes, with the memory scans, it wasn’t just the Anomaly’s Agents that Light had caught; spies from the other three Factions were caught too.
Light was... completely spotless right now, with absolutely no outside spies in their Faction.
It was rare for a Faction that big to be so clean.
And Light—
That too without anyone suspecting them.
After all, right now, Light was only a victim. A victim that had been tormented by an enemy and had no way to retaliate.
What else could the victim possibly do?
Sure, the entire Universe was laughing at Light and pitying them, but in truth, no being, absolutely no being had a possible solution to the problem they were facing.
Not even the Infinities.
Somewhere in their minds, they just considered themselves lucky to not be in Seraphielle’s position.
Not that they would ever admit it.
But yes, in the eyes of the entire Universe, Light was a poor victim, a victim who did not know what to do.
Right now—
No one in the Universe actually suspected Light. Even when Light killed all the traitors and spies inside their territory, not one being suspected them.
They just understood that it was only a desperate act.
But Light—
Light was using this chance to... prepare for the War.
The War between the four Infinities.
A war that was now... inevitable.
Especially now that Anomaly was involved.
Lady Seraphielle had already sensed it. The other three Infinities had no plans of helping them; they were hoping the Anomaly and Light would face each other and were waiting for a result.
And obviously, Seraphielle had no plans to do that.
She had no intention of making everything so easy for them.
So she—
She was preparing for War instead.

The enemy would be crippled.
Seraphielle had also ordered a few of her important worlds to actually stop doing things that made them Anomaly’s targets.
So quite a few Light Worlds now ran on actual justice, worlds where even the powerful were punished for injustice, and the weak and the right...

Already fourteen worlds had left their side, and Lady Seraphielle still hadn’t ’reacted’ to it. If the number continued to rise, it would only be a matter of time before the other Infinities started suspecting Lady Seraphielle of being... too silent.

An Eternal Level Light Born, Araya, walked into a room with a solemn look on her face.
In front of her sat another Light Born, Lucian, another Eternal Level Light Born, and not just any Eternal—
He was the second strongest.
Well—
Now the strongest Light Born.
Yes, after Auren, it was him who was known for his strength, the only Light Born who could actually face Auren and not lose as pathetically as others did.
Lucian was strong, stronger than almost all the Light Borns, and with Auren now out of the picture, his importance only grew more.
But...
Lucian did not like that.
If it was any other situation, a situation where Auren somehow perished or was weakened and he replaced him, he wouldn’t have minded.
But with Light being targeted as strongly as it was right now—
Lucian feared that he too had become a target.
He thought that Auren was taken out because he was the hope of Light.
The strongest being the Anomaly could defeat, so he did.
And now?
That being was him.
If Anomaly targeted him, the Light Borns who now had their hopes on him would feel crushed.
Of course, he was giving himself too much credit.
No Light Born actually held any hopes on him, not when the one stronger than him was defeated without having much of a chance to fight.

Not when the other party was stronger than them and held more power.

Lucian raised his eyebrow.
"It has only been two months since lockdown began.

He commented, letting go of the documents he was reading.
Araya did not say anything, she just stood still, thinking.

Araya answered in a low voice.

They weren’t actually protected.
This was more about protecting Light’s reputation than protecting them, and after Light’s desperate action, it was becoming clearer and clearer.

It was about fear.

Anomaly had already proved that Light’s protection did absolutely nothing to stop him.
It didn’t even slow him down.
They were scared of Light itself, of what Light might do if they decided to leave.

There was only so much fear could actually make people do.
After constant suppression in almost every way, almost every single world would leave.
It was only a matter of time.

chapters.title: Chapter 2287: The Fifth Infinity.
paragraphs: "It’s Lord Orravyn, he and the other Infinities wish to talk."
Lord Light reported. He seemed frustrated and... afraid.
How could he not be?

They had been planning, they had been making sure that every single thing remained a secret, and that they would make the first move before anyone could realize. Lady Seraphielle was the one who was supposed to contact the other Infinities, not the other way around.
Lord Light’s mind had already started spinning.
Why do they wish to talk?
Why only now?
What were they trying to do?
Do they... know?

He couldn’t help but think more and more strongly about that last possibility, because if the other Infinities knew and had been preparing proper defense, then the element of surprise they had been hoping to get would be ruined and they...
Their position would be much, much worse.
Light needed this, desperately.
So the more Lord Light thought about it, the more stuck he felt.
Seraphielle, on the other hand, was much calmer. She looked at Lord Light and—
"Did they say something?"

She asked, but honestly, she already knew the answer. The Infinities were like her; they wouldn’t say anything. So even before Lord Light could shake his head, Seraphielle had already stood up from her throne and looked in a particular direction.
A direction where she could sense the other three were gathered.
She then took a step forward and she—
"Be prepared to move the moment I give the command."
"Lady Seraphielle, the preparation—"
"I will stall, but if I fail, move with whatever we have. Leave the lower-level worlds, focus on the stronger ones."
"I understand."
Lord Light nodded and Seraphielle disappeared.
Lord Light stood at the temple for a few seconds, preparing himself for the grand War that could start any moment now.
Then, he began communicating with other Light Borns, giving orders to rush the preparations even further.
Even the Light Borns who had been resting after working tirelessly were sent to work again.
On the other side, Seraphielle appeared in a giant room with a ridiculously large table in the middle, the same room where the Infinities always held their discussions.
The only difference was that this time, it was the actual Infinities who had gathered, not their Wills.

A rare sight, one that for a moment made Seraphielle pause as she glanced at the beings sitting in the room. Only for a very small second, of course; she then quickly shook her head and sat on her seat.
Silence fell in the room, no one spoke, almost as if the four strongest beings in the Universe were trying to silently read each other.
Seraphielle, of course, had no complaints; she was hoping to stall for a few hours anyway, she wouldn’t mind spending a few moments in these foolish games.

Minutes passed by in moments. For any other being in the Universe, sitting at the table in silence for this long would make them lose their minds. Even beings like Auren, or the strongest Supreme Borns of other Supreme Worlds, would be the same.
The Infinities, however, did not care.
They just waited—
Until one of them had no choice but to speak.
And that one became Orravyn.
"I apologize for calling all of you out all of a sudden."
The Infinity of Eternity spoke, looking at the people present in the room.
"Bah!"
The Infinity of Darkness, Ul’Thakar, shook his head in his usual aggressive tone.
"Don’t spout something you do not mean!"
Then, he turned towards Seraphielle and his grin widened.
"Not to mention if there is someone who should apologize, it is her."
Seraphielle tilted her head in confusion when she heard those words.
"What do you mean?"
She asked directly.
"You have to ask?"
Ul’Thakar seemed surprised.
Then, he shook his hand dismissively and—
"As if you don’t know what I am talking about. Don’t play innocent, Seraphielle. It is disgusting."
"I do not know."
Seraphielle answered in an assertive tone.
Ul’Thakar looked at her for a moment and—
"You closed your worlds. It affected the Universal Scale; countless have suffered. For someone who screams peace, happiness and whatnot—
It was quite a selfish move."
He spoke. For a moment, Seraphielle sighed in relief.
They did not know.
She thought inwardly.
Like Lord Light, she too had the same fear in her head, but seeing that even Ul’Thakar did not mention it, it was clear that they didn’t know.
Or...
It could be that Ul’Thakar did not know, but others did.
Seraphielle doubted Orravyn, but of course, she didn’t say or show anything, she wasn’t foolish enough to give her plan away through her expressions.
She was... a few eras too old to make a mistake like that.
"I did what was necessary."
Seraphielle answered. There was this annoyed tone in her voice that she tried to hide, but couldn’t, and Ul’Thakar enjoyed every moment of it.
"Your actions are only making things easier for Anomaly. You are proving to the Universe that the Infinities are unable to stop him. You are ruining our reputation."
He began giving a lecture.
"If you have a better idea, I am all ears. For someone who has done nothing all this while, you sure have a lot to speak."
Seraphielle snorted as she closed her eyes; it was clear she did not wish to talk about this matter any longer.
"Nothing? I sent help! You sent them back, that isn’t my fault! They were quite good men!"
Ul’Thakar answered; he felt wronged.
"If you consider those worms to be ’quite good’, then I was mistaken to expect help from you."
Seraphielle answered, without looking at Ul’Thakar.
Ul’Thakar’s crimson eyes shined.
But before he could say anything else—
"That is enough."
Another voice spoke.
It was the Infinity of Balance, Equarios.
He then looked at Seraphielle and—
"You are having a difficult time."
He spoke with a gentle, compassionate tone, almost as if he was actually worried about her and felt bad.
Of course, Seraphielle didn’t buy it.
No one did.
Seraphielle just turned towards Orravyn, completely ignoring the Infinity of Balance and—
"Did you call us here for these foolish talks?"
She asked.

While stalling here was a good thing for her, Seraphielle did not wish to look too suspicious. She would normally never entertain the other Infinities having ’fun’ because of her situation, so she couldn’t possibly keep this conversation going or these old monsters would notice something.
Orravyn looked at Seraphielle for a moment and didn’t say anything, and Seraphielle...
She let out a big sigh in disappointment—
"I do not have the time for these games, Orravyn.
Unlike the three of you, I actually have an enemy I need to deal with."
And she stood up, prepared to leave.
"Heh, we are seeing how you are dealing with your enemy, the entire Universe is seeing it."
Ul’Thakar grinned; the superiority and mockery were apparent in his tone. Seraphielle looked at him with her same usual calm and—
"Then you and the entire Universe can continue watching, because once I deal with the Anomaly and capture him alive—
Don’t think you will receive anything out of it."
"Capture him alive?"
Ul’Thakar laughed even louder.
"Bold words for someone who doesn’t even know which of her worlds would be attacked next."
"We will see about that."
Seraphielle just shrugged and turned around, preparing to leave, but before she could—
"Seraphielle, please stop."
Orravyn finally spoke up.
"Just let her go, who cares?"
Ul’Thakar snorted.
"Why have you called us anyway?"
The Infinity of Darkness asked. Equarios nodded too; he wanted to know as well. Orravyn looked at them and—
"The Fifth Infinity contacted."
He revealed.
"What...?"
This time, even Seraphielle, who was actually prepared to leave, turned around, somewhat surprised.
The Fifth Infinity...?
He called?
Why now of all times?
She couldn’t help but wonder.
This would change everything; none of her immediate plans included the appearance of the Fifth Infinity. What was she supposed to do now!?
She didn’t know what he was like, neither could she predict his actions, not to mention he had connections with the Anomaly too.
The only person who might actually be aware of her plans was the Anomaly; what if the Anomaly knew and the Fifth Infinity was acting on it?
All these questions appeared in her mind.
And it wasn’t just her; the other two Infinities who heard the news for the first time had countless thoughts in their heads.
After all, they too had plans of their own—plans that would all be ruined if they added another player into this game.
"Are you sure it was him?"
Equarios narrowed his eyes.
And Orravyn—he did not answer, he just waved his hand and a crystal ball appeared in front of him, hovering in the air.
"It was left in front of my World a few hours ago; I could not trace it back."
He spoke as he gently touched the crystal, then—
He activated it. The crystal projected a screen in the air, and on that screen—
There was that face.
The face the Infinities wouldn’t forget.
Azriel Ruinous.

chapters.title: Chapter 2288: You think too highly of yourself.
paragraphs: "It was left in front of my World a few hours ago, I could not trace it back."
Orravyn spoke as he gently touched the crystal and activated it. The crystal glowed and a screen appeared in the air.
"How primitive."
Ul’Thakar snorted in disdain.
No one else reacted to those words; their focus was on the screen and there—
He appeared.
The man who once stared at them with an arrogance they had never seen or experienced before.
A face so full of pure ego, arrogance, and superiority that for a moment, even the Infinities were taken aback.
And that face—
It hadn’t changed one bit.
Even now, when he was seeing them directly.
And of course, the Infinities did not like that one bit, especially someone as arrogant as Ul’Thakar; he felt that he was looking at a mirror and he hated that feeling.
"It is always amusing to see how arrogant one can be when they hide behind a screen."
Unable to hold back, he commented. Then his crimson eyes glowed strongly as he grinned—
"And satisfying when the same arrogance disappears when they are standing face to face."
A provocation.
A direct provocation, and right now, none of the other Infinities stopped Ul’Thakar. They waited. They wanted to see how the Fifth Infinity would react.
For a moment, the room was silent again.
And the Fifth Infinity, his blood-red eyes fell on Darkness and without a single change in his expression—
"A pack of four wolves and a dragon—
Who do you think has the right to look more arrogant?"
Azriel Ruinous opened his mouth and in an instant—
The room chilled.
This time, even the other Infinities reacted. They had been silent, yes, but this did not mean they had no ego of their own.
These were Infinities; their egos were the strongest the Universe had to offer.
In an instant, Orravyn moved, trying to sense Azriel’s location, and after about a second, he grinned—
"Difficult to answer that question when the ’dragon’ is the one hiding."
The rest of the Infinities smiled disdainfully as well, as if they didn’t even like the fact that they had to spend their time on this man.
Azriel, on the other hand, looked at Orravyn and—
"Do mortals know where their God actually is?"
He asked.
Orravyn frowned, but before he could say anything, Azriel’s blood-red eyes glowed—a shade deeper than Ul’Thakar’s—and—
"Think of it in the same way.
The Gods do not consider mortals worthy enough to appear in front of them.
You show yourself when youconverseat the same level—
Not when you are answering a prayer."
Azriel answered in that same arrogant tone and once again, a deathly cold silence fell in the room.
The Infinities reacted to those words.
Their egos were wounded—not just Orravyn’s or Ul’Thakar’s, all four of them were the same. After all, they knew that Azriel wasn’t just saying those words to the two; he was talking to them all.
"Answering a prayer...?"
Seraphielle muttered in a somewhat lost, shocked voice. Never in her life did she imagine someone saying those words to her.
"Is that not what it was?
A few years ago I heard a cry for help, something like how you lot couldn’t deal with an enemy and needed help.
I answered.
Like a God does."
"Five years later?"
Ul’Thakar grinned, wanting to imply how big of a coward Azriel was for showing up five years later, but—
"Since when do Gods answer prayers the moment it’s requested? Gods move when they feel convenient. I had things to do before, so I figured you would be able to hold on till then."
Azriel paused, then he looked at Seraphielle and—

He commented, and Seraphielle—
She felt her mouth twitching. She closed her eyes, a sign that she no longer wanted to talk about this matter.
But did Azriel care?
He didn’t give a rat’s ass.
"To lose... three hundred, was it?
Three hundred worlds to a single enemy and not causing any harm to the enemy at all. If it were me, I would have killed myself out of embarrassment by now."
He continued to speak.
"But then again, I suppose you did hold off for five years.
You didn’t die. I congratulate you for that.
I believe with the way things stand, that alone is an achie—"
"That is enough."
Before Azriel could complete, Seraphielle spoke up. Her aura flared—enough for many beings in the Universe to feel it, especially the Light Borns.
Light Borns, still far away from the meeting room, frowned.
"Is that... a signal?"
He wondered in his head, but he shook his head.
Lady Seraphielle had already explained what the signal would be; she wouldn’t change it at the last moment.
This must be something else.
Someone...
Someone must have angered her, enough to make her react in this manner.
Who was it...?
Lord Light wondered in his head and instantly started suspecting Ul’Thakar.
Back in the Infinities’ Meeting Room, Seraphielle glared at Azriel—a look that would make most beings in the Universe flinch, cower, and shake in fear.
But Azriel stood still, as if he felt nothing.
And that only annoyed Seraphielle even further.
"You were the one who protected the Anomaly back then."
She began to speak; her tone had lost the gentle touch she usually had.
"You knew him before we did, younurturedhim.
Are we right to believe that he is with you?"
"He is not."
Azriel shook his head.
"And we should believe you, why?"
Seraphielle narrowed her eyes and at that question—
Azriel directly looked into her eyes and—
"What gave you the idea that I care?
Believe whatever you want.
I am not the one standing with no information regarding the enemy.
You called me, not the other way around. Keep that in your mind."
Again.
Silence.
The Infinities did not know how to proceed from here. It was clear that both sides had strong egos, and if none of them gave in, even a little—
This conversation wouldn’t go anywhere.
The fact that this man is probably the only being who can tell them about the Anomaly wasn’t false either. Whatever it may be, the Fifth Infinity was their only connection to the Anomaly.

If they wanted to find anything about the Anomaly—which they did, because whether they believed it or not, the Anomaly was, at some level, a threat—had he been targeting any one of them like he was targeting Light,
They too wouldn’t know what to do.
Plus, the fear that the Anomaly might disappear and return to his own Universe wasn’t without grounds either—
The Infinities wanted to avoid that.
So they needed the Fifth Infinity.
And considering all that, Equarios, who had been silent all this while, spoke up, trying to act as a bridge.
"We have no information about the enemy. Does that mean you do?"
He asked.
And when he spoke, he made sure his tone didn’t sound like he was looking down on the Fifth Infinity. It was easy to sense that was the core of the conflict; he wanted to avoid that.
Azriel sensed his intentions and—
"I have met him before, yes."
Azriel nodded.
"At that time, I did not know what he was or what he was capable of."
"So he fooled you."
Ul’Thakar pointed almost instantly.
Azriel looked at him and—
"I didn’t care enough to notice."
"That’s a convenient excuse."
Ul’Thakar laughed, and Azriel, who was turning his gaze back to Equarios to have a conversation, turned back to him and—
"If I cared about every single being I encounter, I would care too much.
Don’t think you are any different.
If you are lying to me or trying to fool me, you can—since I wouldn’t bother noticing. It is the same sense of insignificance you feel when you deal with those below you.
Whatever plans or schemes you might have, you do not have the capability to hurt or even affect me,
So why would I bother?
I have better things to invest my time in."

Another wave of silence spread, and this one was far more tense than the others. It was the first time any being had talked to the Four Supremes with such tone and arrogance. Maybe it was a habit or whatever, but even they themselves did not use that tone when they talked to each other.
So this was...
This was clearly out of the line, for every one of them.
"You think too highly of yourself."
Ul’Thakar spoke, and now there was no hint of amusement in his voice.
"Come here, let’s see if your limbs can back up your mouth."
He challenged directly, and before Azriel could say anything—
"You know what, fuck it, I already know what you are going to say.
So tell me where you are and I’ll come to you, alone."
Ul’Thakar stood up, and as he did, the entire room they were in turned... darker.

The other Infinities’ faces turned stiff; they could see it as well. Ul’Thakar was serious. He was annoyed to the point where things might go south, and while the entire interaction would benefit them and they wanted it to continue—
They also knew the Fifth Infinity was a new player—
They did not wish to pursue anything without any plans, so—
"That is enough."
Equarios spoke up, stopping Ul’Thakar.
"We still need information about the Anomaly.
Don’t act rashly."

chapters.title: Chapter 2289: I do not trust you four.
paragraphs: "That is enough.
We still need information about the Anomaly.
Don’t act rashly."
Equarios spoke as he stared at Ul’Thakar and then Azriel. From his tone, he seemed like he was talking to both of them, but it was clear that his message was for Ul’Thakar.
Ul’Thakar understood that as well and he took control over his temper, a temper that had overtaken him for a very small moment there.
He looked at Equarios, who nodded at him again without any change in his expression, then he looked back at Azriel.
"You have a way with words."
He commented.
"I know people with a far sharper tongue, you need to control your temper if you wish to encounter him."
Azriel answered, looking at Ul’Thakar.
"Are you... talking about the Anomaly?"
Orravyn asked.

After all, he couldn’t imagine many people talking to Ul’Thakar the way Azriel did. He had also personally seen every single recording the Anomaly had spread in the Universe in hopes of learning something about him. His plan didn’t work, the Anomaly didn’t reveal much about himself in the recordings, but if there was one thing he did learn about the foreign monster, it was that he... was annoying.
And not just slightly annoying or a nuisance, the Anomaly was... charmingly annoying. He had a way to get under people’s skin without doing anything.
Orravyn hadn’t forgotten that same creepily calm smile at the end of every single one of his recordings, like everything was going according to the plan.

He, who wasn’t even at the receiving end of those recordings and wasn’t dealing with any damage, felt his frustration boiling up. He could only imagine what Seraphielle must have felt while she watched those.
It wouldn’t be surprising if the Infinity of Light actually snapped and did something out of expectation.
While Orravyn was thinking all this, Azriel looked at him and he—
"Yes."
He nodded at his question.
"So you do know him."
Orravyn pointed out.
"I already told you that."
Azriel frowned, as if he couldn’t understand why the man was talking like he had revealed a universal secret when he had already made it so obvious.
Seeing his expression, Orravyn felt his mouth twitch, but he didn’t show it. He just stared at him and—
"What can you tell us about him?"
"There is nothing much."
Azriel spoke.
"As I said, he was merely an outsider in my eyes, someone who came to my world as a mercenary, he sought my permission to trade, I gave him the permission."
"That’s it?"
Orravyn frowned.
"That is it."
Azriel nodded with a convincing look on his face, but—
"You protected him.
You hid him from us.
Your relationship doesn’t seem that simple."

Seraphielle spoke as she looked into Azriel’s eyes. Azriel looked at her and for a moment, they both were silent. No matter how desperately Seraphielle tried to hide it, the Anomaly’s existence bothered her.
She wanted to know more about him and find a way to deal with him, and now that it was finally in front of her, she was getting more desperate.
The Fifth Infinity, however, didn’t react to her words, at least not as strongly as she thought he would.

"He offered me a trade, something I couldn’t refuse. And in return, he asked me to protect him from some ’eyes’. I didn’t even know those eyes would be... you people, I simply held up my end of the deal."
"You knew it was us and yet you still didn’t find him suspicious?"
Seraphielle asked.
"Hmm? Why would I? You are the Four Supremes, don’t you have your eyes on the entire Universe? You lot are nosy and it is not uncommon for beings to try and hide things from you."
"The Universe reacted to him, even back then. As an Infinity, you should have been able to sense its anger, yet you still helped him.
Did you not, for once, doubt why even the Universe is reacting to his movements? That there must be something suspicious about him?"
Light asked another question.
"Surprising the Universe isn’t difficult.
You should know it better than I do."
Azriel’s answer was direct.

Seraphielle did not deny his words either, there was no point, not when they too were hiding things from the Universe’s Will. They also knew that as an Infinity who was no different from them, the Fifth Infinity too must be hiding things from the Universe, so yes, at some level, agitating the Universe wasn’t a difficult thing.
It just showed you were... bad at hiding.
Or at least, that’s what any one of them would have thought if something like that had happened with them.

But even then, even if they had thought of that, they would have investigated a ’foreign mercenary who came to their world for trade’, they might even have captured him alive and read his memories, just to make sure he was clear.

After all, as simple as it sounded, fooling the Universe wasn’t exactly a... breeze. At least not if you are not an Infinity. If someone other than an Infinity had pulled something like that, they would have definitely read his memories and investigated him thoroughly.
So...
Either the Fifth Infinity wasn’t as sly as he showed himself to be.
Or he was lying.
About the Anomaly, about everything he knew about him.
And the Infinities, they were leaning towards the latter.
"What was it?"
Suddenly, Orravyn asked a question. Azriel glanced at him and Orravyn—
"The trade he offered you, the thing you couldn’t refuse.
What was it that made even an Infinity move?"
"I will not answer that."
Azriel shook his head and the Infinities... they turned silent.
"Why is that?"
Orravyn asked after about a minute of silence passed.
"I have my reasons."
Azriel kept his answer vague.
"That is... suspicious."
Orravyn narrowed his eyes.
"I have no reason to share personal information with you."
"What world do you come from, Fifth Infinity?"
Suddenly, Seraphielle asked another question, but—
"What makes you think I will tell you that?"
Azriel asked.
"Because you know where we are, we do not know where you are. That is not fair, don’t you think?"
Seraphielle reasoned.

"You were the ones who announced yourselves to the Universe, created your factions and played whatever little games you have been playing. You made your presence known, I had no part in it. I see no reason for me to give information I have been hiding in exchange for something that has been public since the beginning of time."
"Those who hide from the Universe usually are up to no good."
Seraphielle narrowed her eyes.
"What you think does not matter to me."
Azriel just shrugged.
Seraphielle narrowed her eyes but then—
"How did the Anomaly find you in the first place?"
Orravyn asked.
"You said he came to your world as a mercenary, how did he know it was your world? How did he know when even we didn’t?
Don’t say it was a coincidence that he just happened to be there."
"I don’t know."
Azriel, however, shrugged even harder.
"It can be a coincidence, highly unlikely, yes, but the chances are still there."
"You are not giving us anything to work with."
Equarios spoke directly, feeling slightly frustrated.
"Why did you contact us?"
He asked.
"You called me."
Azriel repeated his answer.
"Yes, I understand that and you answered us.
But why?
You know what we wanted from you from the very beginning, information about the Anomaly and support.
But from your words, it is clear that you have no intention of telling us anything, then why contact us?
Or are you just bored?"
"Iamtelling you everything I know."
Azriel defended himself.
"You know that as much as we do."
Equarios didn’t believe him, but—
"I am not lying."
Azriel spoke with a convincing look.
"I do not know much about the Anomaly, I already said what I told you. Other than that, I do not even know as much as you do simply because I did not matter."
"Do you... not feel threatened by him?"
Equarios asked with a curious look on his face.
"No."
Azriel shook his head directly.
"Why so confident?"
"He has been in my presence.
He would know better."
The answer was direct and the arrogance oozing out of it was almost... frustrating.
"Come here."
Suddenly, Ul’Thakar, who had been silent all this while, spoke again.
"Come to us, or call us.
Anywhere you desire.
Let’s have a face-to-face chat, with no deceptions, nothing."
The Infinity of Darkness offered, but—
"No."
Azriel shook his head. The Infinities frowned. Azriel, already knowing what they were going to ask, answered directly.
"I do not trust you four."
"What does that mean?"
Ul’Thakar narrowed his eyes.
"I have reasons to believe one of you is with the Anomaly."
"What...? Weare working with the Anomaly?"
Ul’Thakar’s expression changed.
"His actions are too convenient for you otherwise. It doesn’t make sense to target just one faction. Especially when all factions are as rotten as the one being targeted, just in a different manner."
"He is attacking one of us because he wishes to divide us."
Orravyn reasoned. Azriel looked at him and—
"Or he is doing what one of you wants him to do and weaken Light’s faction."

Or at least, that’s what any one of them would have thought if something like that had happened with them.

But even then, even if they had thought of that, they would have investigated a ’foreign mercenary who came to their world for trade’, they might even have captured him alive and read his memories, just to make sure he was clear.
After all, as simple as it sounded, fooling the Universe wasn’t exactly a... breeze.
At least not if you are not an Infinity.
If someone other than an Infinity had pulled something like that, they would have definitely read his memories and investigated him thoroughly.
So...
Either the Fifth Infinity wasn’t as sly as he showed himself to be.
Or he was lying.
About the Anomaly, about everything he knew about him.
And the Infinities, they were leaning towards the latter.
"What was it?"
Suddenly, Orravyn asked a question.
Azriel glanced at him and Orravyn—
"The trade he offered you, the thing you couldn’t refuse.
What was it that made even an Infinity move?"
"I will not answer that."
Azriel shook his head and the Infinities... they turned silent.
"Why is that?"
Orravyn asked after about a minute of silence passed.
"I have my reasons."
Azriel kept his answer vague.
"That is... suspicious."
Orravyn narrowed his eyes.
"I have no reason to share personal information with you."
"What world do you come from, Fifth Infinity?"
Suddenly, Seraphielle asked another question, but—
"What makes you think I will tell you that?"
Azriel asked.
"Because you know where we are, we do not know where you are.
That is not fair, don’t you think?"
Seraphielle reasoned.
"You were the ones who announced yourselves to the Universe, created your factions and played whatever little games you have been playing.
You made your presence known, I had no part in it.
I see no reason for me to give information I have been hiding in exchange for something that has been public since the beginning of time."
"Those who hide from the Universe usually are up to no good."
Seraphielle narrowed her eyes.
"What you think does not matter to me."
Azriel just shrugged.
Seraphielle narrowed her eyes but then—
"How did the Anomaly find you in the first place?"
Orravyn asked.
"You said he came to your world as a mercenary, how did he know it was your world?
How did he know when even we didn’t?
Don’t say it was a coincidence that he just happened to be there."
"I don’t know."
Azriel, however, shrugged even harder.
"It can be a coincidence, highly unlikely, yes, but the chances are still there."
"You are not giving us anything to work with."
Equarios spoke directly, feeling slightly frustrated.
"Why did you contact us?"
He asked.
"You called me."
Azriel repeated his answer.
"Yes, I understand that and you answered us.
But why?
You know what we wanted from you from the very beginning, information about the Anomaly and support.
But from your words, it is clear that you have no intention of telling us anything, then why contact us?
Or are you just bored?"
"Iamtelling you everything I know."
Azriel defended himself.
"You know that as much as we do."
Equarios didn’t believe him, but—
"I am not lying."
Azriel spoke with a convincing look.
"I do not know much about the Anomaly, I already said what I told you.
Other than that, I do not even know as much as you do simply because I did not matter."
"Do you... not feel threatened by him?"
Equarios asked with a curious look on his face.
"No."
Azriel shook his head directly.
"Why so confident?"
"He has been in my presence.
He would know better."
The answer was direct and the arrogance oozing out of it was almost... frustrating.
"Come here."
Suddenly, Ul’Thakar, who had been silent all this while, spoke again.
"Come to us, or call us.
Anywhere you desire.
Let’s have a face-to-face chat, with no deceptions, nothing."
The Infinity of Darkness offered, but—
"No."
Azriel shook his head.
The Infinities frowned.
Azriel, already knowing what they were going to ask, answered directly.
"I do not trust you four."
"What does that mean?"
Ul’Thakar narrowed his eyes.
"I have reasons to believe one of you is with the Anomaly."
"What...?
Weare working with the Anomaly?"
Ul’Thakar’s expression changed.
"His actions are too convenient for you otherwise.
It doesn’t make sense to target just one faction.
Especially when all factions are as rotten as the one being targeted, just in a different manner."
"He is attacking one of us because he wishes to divide us."
Orravyn reasoned.
Azriel looked at him and—
"Or he is doing what one of you wants him to do and weaken Light’s faction."

chapters.title: Chapter 2290: Prove it.
paragraphs: "His actions are too convenient for it to be otherwise.
He has been constantly targeting just one of the four Factions, he has constantly stated he is doing it to reveal Light’s hypocrisy, I get that.
But I also understand that the other three Factions are no different, all of your factions are rotten to the core.
So why target just one? Especially when he has the power to disappear any time he desires."
Azriel explained his reasoning, something that only made the other Infinities frown, especially Orravyn.
"He is targeting Light because he wants us to think exactly like you are thinking right now.
It is an attempt to divide us."
"Or, he is doing it because one of you ordered him to."
"What...?"
Seraphielle narrowed her eyes. Azriel looked at her and—
"What? Does it not seem too intentional to you? Why target just you? Sure, divide and conquer, that I understand and that very much could be a plan but even then,
Why you? Just because it was convenient? You definitely weren’t the easiest target, neither were you the strongest.
It seemed like you were chosen almost... randomly.
And at the level we are, random is... suspicious."

Orravyn wanted to counter, he wanted to say that Light was chosen because calling out its hypocrisy was easy, that it gave the Anomaly a ’cause’, but he also understood that explaining that would only make the situation worse.
Plus, he knew Seraphielle was no fool either, so while he could see the Fifth Infinity was trying to manipulate her, succeeding in that was an entirely different scenario.
"While according to my theory, your weakening... will not only ease some of the pressure from another Infinity.
Your fall will also benefit them, at an individual level.

Say Eternity, for example. Before this, Light had the strongest reputation in history, they were considered fair and trustworthy, almost all neutral worlds leaned towards Light, but now that has changed. Now, Eternity has overtaken Light in that regard.
Even when Light Worlds are leaving, their number one choice is the Eternity Faction. That is certainly a motive at some level."
Azriel spoke as he exchanged looks between Seraphielle and Orravyn. The two Infinities also looked at each other, trying to understand what the other was thinking.
Azriel smiled at that and—
"The next is Darkness."
He spoke, looking at Ul’Thakar.
"The relationship between Light and Darkness couldn’t be clearer since... the beginning. If Light is weakened, it is obviously good for Darkness."
He stated the obvious, something both Seraphielle and Ul’Thakar had thought of before.
"The only one I cannot directly link with the situation is Balance, but then again, the information I have on you people is limited, so maybe I am missing something.
It is up to you to decide. I only know that the Four Infinities, the four Leaders of the Universe, beings who have been together for eras, do not trust each other.
And if you do not trust each other, I too have no reason to come to you and put myself in danger, nor do I plan on letting you roam around my world."
"We don’t even know where your world is."
Orravyn spoke, still trying to get something from the conversation.
"As I said, I do not wish to reveal that to you lot."
Azriel had the same answer and this time—
"You talk an awful lot."
Orravyn finally snapped.
"You have been pointing fingers at us ever since the conversation began, you kept saying how you do not trust us.
But in the end—
Aren’t you the most untrustworthy one amongst us all?
You are the one who was first seen with the Anomaly, defending and hiding him from us.
You are the one who is hiding from us and doesn’t wish to reveal where he is or what world he resides in.
You are the one who is trying to sow discord amongst us with your words.
And yet, somehow...
We are the suspicious ones!?"
The Infinity of Eternity raised his voice.
Azriel didn’t react, he just stayed silent, letting the conversation go on and allowing Orravyn to speak whatever he wanted.
"You know what I think?"
And that’s what Orravyn did, he started speaking.
"I think the Anomaly is with you.
He is working for you, he isyour ultimate secret. A secret you forgot to hide from the Universe, so you needed to make a move yourself to make things right, revealing yourself in the process.
The Anomaly is your weapon, a weapon you plan on using against us, to tear us apart and later take what is ours.

You have been watching us for millions of years, craving all that power we hold for yourself, and it makes sense. You are an Infinity, one of the strongest beings in the Universe, youdeservepower, but as strong as you are, you aren’t strong enough to take our power, not with the four of us still at our strongest.
So you plan to weaken us, using the Anomaly. And once we are weakened, that is when you plan on striking.
And today too, your intention isn’t giving us relevant information, it is to divide us, to make us fight amongst ourselves and perish,
So you can come reap the rewards."
Orravyn spoke, looking at Azriel with his hollow eyes.
The other Infinities stared at Azriel too, the directive was clear and Orravyn’s words were quite believable.
They, as Infinities, understood what another Infinity, who wasn’t at their level just because he was born later than them, must feel.
Using the Anomaly and the chaos to fit in and aim for more power was one of the most obvious paths for him.
Something every single one of them would have done.
But now...
Now when his plan was finally revealed—
Things would become much more difficult.
After all, the four of them had no intention of letting a Fifth one come in. They could already imagine the amount of chaos and unpredictability another addition would bring.
Not to mention...
If this being came into existence after Zylarith perished...
That would make him Zylarith’s successor and the last thing they wanted to do was to give a platform to someone who could potentially become another Zylarith in the future.

So yes, the Four Infinities had no intention of letting the Fifth Infinity grow, they would restrict him in every way possible, no matter what it took, even if it required the four of them to come together and move as one.
Yes, they were that serious.
And that could be seen from their faces.
Something Azriel read quite clearly as well and he—
He smiled.
"That is a good story."
He nodded, seemingly satisfied, staring at all the Infinities, then he looked just at Orravyn.
"You must be the one these three listen to, you have quite the say here, I can tell."
"That is quite an obvious and foolish attempt, I am the younges—"
Before Orravyn could say anything, Azriel interrupted.
"So you are saying that I am with the Anomaly and completely disregard my theory of the Anomaly being with one of you, correct?"
"I am not disregarding anything, I am just stating what feels most natural."
Orravyn answered calmly.
"And what if I prove you wrong? What if I prove I am not with the Anomaly?"
And there it was.
Orravyn paused, not saying anything.
But that didn’t mean every single person there was silent.
"How will you prove it?"
Seraphielle asked, her eyes lingering on Orravyn for a few more milliseconds than normal.
"I have my ways."
Azriel answered, then he looked into Seraphielle’s eyes and—
"But if I do prove I am right, then you know what that means, correct?"
He asked.

And this time, Seraphielle’s eyes changed. She once again looked at Orravyn, the man who was the first to shift all the blame on the Fifth, the one who benefited the most in this Anomaly situation and the man who... had the means to back up a being like the Anomaly, without anyone knowing.
If the Fifth was indeed right then Orravyn—
He would become the most suspicious.
"Seraphielle, do not listen to him. You are only helping him achieve what he wants."
Orravyn, understanding Seraphielle’s look, spoke directly.
Seraphielle didn’t say anything, she just continued to stare at the Infinity of Eternity and Orravyn clenched his fists.
"Prove it."
He spoke as he turned towards the Fifth Infinity.
"Prove that you are not with the Anomaly, I too wish to see how you are going to prove that."
It was clear what he wanted to do. Any proof the Fifth would have, he would refute it. After all, unless the Anomaly himself made it clear, there was nothing certain—
Except...
"Alright."
Azriel nodded.
Then, he raised his hand and—
THUNDER THUNDER THUNDER
RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
The Universe reacted, not out of anger, out of... happiness.
Out of... familiarity.
And the moment the Infinities realized what was happening, their eyes widened in shock.
The Universe’s Child.
They...
They were talking to the man the very Universe had chosen to be its...Hero.
